Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:10:1.hebrew: ואפילו ע"י חופה - דהא לאו בת נישואין היא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:10:1.english: And even by means of a wedding canopy - For she is not a woman fit for marriage.

Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:11:1.hebrew: משום דעולא - דאמרי' בריש פירקין (קידושין דף ה.): שמא ימזגו לה כוס בבית אביה, ותשקה לאחיה ולאחותיה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:11:1.english: Due to Ulla - As we said at the beginning of this chapter (Kiddushin 5a): Perhaps they will mix a cup for her in her father's house, and she will give it to her brother and to her sister to drink.

Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:12:1.hebrew: לא שייר בקנינה - אחר שנתן הכסף, אין הקנין חסר כלום:
Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:12:1.english: He did not leave out [anything] in her acquisition - After he gave the money, the acquisition is not lacking anything.

Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:12:2.hebrew: הכא שייר בקנינה - דאכתי מיחסרה מסירה לחופה, לענין ליורשה וליטמא לה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:12:2.english: Here he left out [part of] her acquisition - For she still lacks the handing over to the chuppah (wedding canopy), with respect to his inheriting her and becoming ritually impure for her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:13:1.hebrew: רבינא אמר - מהכא ליכא למיפשט דנישואין עושה, דהא אפילו אירוסין עושה אכלה מדאורייתא, וכסף נמי מדאורייתא אכלה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:13:1.english: Ravina said - From here, one cannot resolve [the question] whether marriage [i.e., nisuin] makes [her eligible to eat teruma], for even betrothal [alone] makes [her eligible, so that] she eats [teruma] by Torah law; and with money [alone] as well, she eats by Torah law.

Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:13:2.hebrew: ומדרבנן הוא דשלח ליה - הא דשלח ליה לאוסרה בתרומה, מדרבנן הוא דאסר לה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:13:2.english: And it is by rabbinic law that he sent to him - That which he sent to him, to forbid her from teruma, it is by rabbinic law that he forbade her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:14:1.hebrew: משום סימפון - שמא ימצא בה מום, ונמצאו קידושי טעות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:14:1.english: Because of an annulling factor [simfon] - Lest a blemish be found in her, and the betrothal turn out to have been a mistaken one:

Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:14:2.hebrew: סימפון - כל דבר המבטל דבר, קרוי סימפון שלו. כגון, שובר הוי סימפון של שטר, בשנים אוחזין (ב"מ כ.). וכאן קורא סימפון דבר המבטל את הקידושין, או את המקח של עבד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:14:2.english: Simfon - Anything that nullifies something is called its "simfon." For example, a receipt is the simfon of a document, in [the chapter] "Shnayim Ochazin" (Bava Metzia 20a). And here, [the Gemara] calls "simfon" a thing that nullifies the betrothal, or the purchase of a slave.

Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:14:3.hebrew: ומדרבנן הוא דשלח ליה - הא דשלח ליה לאוסרה בתרומה, מדרבנן הוא דאסר לה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:14:3.english: And it is from the Rabbis that he sent to him - That which he sent to him, to forbid her from teruma, it is by rabbinic enactment that he forbade it to her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:14:4.english: Do you not know - [This is stated] as a rhetorical question of astonishment:

Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:15:1.hebrew: זו שביאתה מאכילתה - דבנישאת מודה, דלא חיישינן לסימפון, דאין אדם שותה בכוס אלא אם כן בודקו וידע וקבל עליו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:15:1.english: This one, whose intercourse allows her to partake - For [regarding a woman] who has been married, [the Tanna] concedes that we are not concerned about simfon, since a person does not drink from a cup unless he has first examined it, knows [its condition], and has accepted it upon himself:

Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:15:2.hebrew: אבל מה אעשה כו' - ולקמיה פריך מאי בינייהו, הואיל וסוף סוף לא אכלה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:15:2.english: But what can I do, etc. - And later [the Gemara] asks: What is the difference between them, since ultimately she does not eat [teruma]?

Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:1:1.hebrew: לטמא משכב תחתון כעליון - שעושה בועלה מושב ומשכב, אפי' עשר מצעות. אבל לא להיות אב הטומאה לטמא אדם וכלים כמשכבה של נדה עצמה, אלא לטמא אוכלין ומשקין, כעליונו של זב. וכן מפרש לה במס' נדה (דף לב:). אבל פחותה מבת שלש שנים אינה מטמאה את בועלה אלא טומאת ערב, כנוגע בעלמא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:1:1.english: To render impure a lower mishkav like the upper one - For [the menstruant] makes the one who has intercourse with her into a seat and a bed, even [if there are] ten mattresses [between them]. But [this is] not so that he becomes a primary source of impurity (avi avot hatumah), rendering people and vessels impure like the bed of the menstruant herself, but rather to render food and liquids impure, like the upper one of a zav. And so it is explained in tractate Niddah (32b). But [a girl] younger than three years old does not render the one who has intercourse with her impure, except with impurity until evening, like one who merely touches [a source of impurity].

Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:2:1.hebrew: נישאת לכהן - קס"ד שנכנסה לחופה לנישואין, אוכלת בתרומה. אבל פחותה מבת ג' שנים, אין חופתה מאכילתה, הואיל ואין ביאתה ביאה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:2:1.english: If she marries a priest - It enters one's mind [to say] that if she entered the chuppa for marriage, she may eat teruma. But [a girl] younger than three years old — her chuppa does not entitle her to eat [teruma], since her act of intercourse is not considered intercourse.

Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:2:2.hebrew: והיא פטורה - לפי שאינה בת עונשין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:2:2.english: And she is exempt - Because she is not subject to punishments.

Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:3:1.hebrew: אי הני נישואין - האי דקתני מתקדשת בביאה, דתנא ברישא, אי לכהן הוי נישואין - אוכלת בתרומה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:3:1.english: If these are marriage - This [woman] who is betrothed through intercourse, as was taught in the first clause: If [this betrothal] is to a priest, [and it constitutes marriage], she eats teruma.

Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:5:1.hebrew: שאין ביאתה מאכילתה - אם בא עליה כהן ולא קנאה בכסף, אינה אוכלת, דבעינן "קנין כספו". וקדושין נמי לא תפסי בה, שתהא מקודשת לו בביאתה, שהרי היא כחמור עם הדומה לחמור:
Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:5:1.english: Whose intercourse does not allow her to eat - If a priest had relations with her and did not acquire her with money, she does not eat teruma, since we require "the purchase of his money." And betrothal also does not take effect with her, so that she would be betrothed to him through her intercourse, for she is like a donkey with one who resembles a donkey:

Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:5:2.hebrew: כספה מאכילתה - דכתיב (ויקרא כב) קנין כספו הוא יאכל בו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:5:2.english: Her money allows her to partake - For it is written (Leviticus 22): "One who is acquired by his money, he may eat of it."

Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:5:3.hebrew: זו שביאתה מאכילתה - קס"ד השתא דביאה עושה נישואין, כדמפרש ואזיל. ונישאת, פשיטא ליה דאכלה, דנפקא ליה בספרי: מכל טהור בביתך יאכל אותו. והך דבן בג בג, התם תני לה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:5:3.english: This one, whose intercourse allows her to eat - The thought now is that intercourse effects marriage, as [the Gemara] goes on to explain. And [once] she is married, it is obvious to [the Tanna] that she eats [teruma], as this is derived in the Sifrei: "Everyone who is pure in your house may eat it" (Numbers 18:11). And as for this [teaching] of Ben Bag Bag, there [in the Sifrei] it is taught.

Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:6:1.hebrew: היכי דמי - דיליף כסף מביאה: אי נימא ביאה שלאחר חופה, ויליף מיניה כסף שהכניסה אחר כך לחופה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:6:1.english: What are the circumstances? - [That is, in a case where] he derives money from intercourse: if we say [it is] intercourse that takes place after the wedding canopy, and he derives from it [a case of] money [betrothal] after which he subsequently brought her into the canopy:

Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:6:2.hebrew: בתרוייהו אכלה - ומאי "אבל מה אעשה" דקאמר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:6:2.english: In both she may eat - So what is [the meaning of] "but what can I do," that [the Gemara] says?

Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:7:1.hebrew: אלא בביאה שע"י חופה - וקא יליף מיניה כסף שלא על ידי חופה. היכי יליף לה מיניה? הכא תרתי, והכא חדא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:7:1.english: Rather, [it refers to] intercourse by means of a canopy - and [the Gemara] derives from it [the law of] money without a canopy. How can one derive it from it? Here [in intercourse] there are two [stages], and here [in money] there is one.

Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:8:1.hebrew: מאי שנא - מה שונה ביאה דפשיטא ליה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:8:1.english: What is different - about intercourse, that it is obvious to him?

Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:8:2.hebrew: ומאי שנא - בקידושי כסף, דמספקא ליה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 10b:8:2.english: And what is different - [in betrothal through] money, that he is uncertain:

Tosafot on Kiddushin 10b:10:1.hebrew: ומה שפחה כנענית וכו' זו שביאתה מאכילתה בתרומה אינו דין שכספה מאכילתה - וא"ת: ונימא "יבמה תוכיח, שביאתה מאכילתה ואין כספה מאכילתה; אף אני אביא ארוסה"? ויש לומר, דהאי ק"ו אינו כ"א גלוי מלתא בעלמא, דארוסה מקרי קנין כספו כמו שפחה; הלכך לא שייך למיפרך "יוכיח". עי"ל דליכא למימר "יבמה תוכיח", דאיכא למיפרך: מה ליבמה, שכן אינה נקנית בכסף! תאמר באשה שנקנית בכסף, דין הוא שתאכל בתרומה על ידי כסף:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 10b:10:1.english: "If a Canaanite maidservant..." etc. "[Then] this one, whose intercourse allows her to partake of teruma — is it not logical that her money allows her to partake?" - And if you say: Let us say, "A yevama (a widow awaiting levirate marriage) will prove [the point], for her intercourse allows her to partake [of teruma], yet her money does not allow her to partake; so too I will bring a betrothed woman [as a counterexample]"? One can answer that this kal vachomer (a fortiori argument) is nothing but a mere clarification of the matter, for a betrothed woman is called one acquired by his money, like a maidservant; therefore it is not applicable to refute [it by saying], "Let it prove." Alternatively, one can say that it is impossible to say "A yevama will prove," for one can refute: What [proof is there] from a yevama, since she is not acquired with money! Will you say [the same] of a woman who is acquired with money, that it is logical that she should partake of teruma by means of money?

Tosafot on Kiddushin 10b:10:2.hebrew: מה שפחה כנענית שאין ביאתה מאכילתה - מהאי ק"ו ליכא למילף שתהא אשה נקנית בכסף ובשטר, דאיכא למיפרך: מה לשפחה כנענית, שכן יוצאה בכסף, כדפריך לעיל גבי אמה העבריה. אבל לענין אכילת תרומה לא שייך למיפרך הכי:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 10b:10:2.english: "Just as a Canaanite maidservant, whose intercourse does not allow her to partake [of teruma]" - From this kal vachomer one cannot derive that a woman is acquired through money and through a document, for one can refute it: What of a Canaanite maidservant, which is [different] in that she goes out [to freedom] through money, as [the Gemara] challenges above regarding the Hebrew maidservant. But with regard to eating teruma, it is not applicable to refute in this way:

Tosafot on Kiddushin 10b:13:1.hebrew: רבינא אמר מדאורייתא מיפשט פשיטא דאכלה - פי': ורבינא בא לקיים לעולם. אימא לך דביאה אירוסין עושה, ודקאמרת: מאי שנא הכא דפשיטא ליה, ומאי שנא הכא דמספקא ליה — בדאורייתא פשיטא דאכלה, בין בביאה בין בכסף. והא דשלח ליה לאוסרה בתרומה — מדרבנן. ומדרבנן היה ריב"ב דן ק"ו: דבביאה פשיטא ליה דאכלה אפילו מדרבנן, דלא שייך בה חשש סימפון, משום דאין אדם שותה בכוס אלא אם כן בודקו; ומק"ו רוצה לדון דבכסף נמי ליכא למיחש לסימפון, כדמפרש בגמרא:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 10b:13:1.english: Ravina said: By Torah law it is obvious to him that she may partake - Explanation: Ravina comes to uphold [the earlier position] entirely. [He says:] I will tell you that intercourse effects betrothal; and as for what you asked — what is different here, that it is obvious to him, and what is different there, that he is uncertain — by Torah law it is obvious that she may partake, whether [betrothed] through intercourse or through money. And as for what he sent him, to forbid her from teruma — [that is] by rabbinic law. And with respect to the rabbinic law, Ribav (Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava) was reasoning by a kal vachomer (a fortiori argument): that in the case of intercourse it is obvious to him that she may partake even by rabbinic law, since the concern of a simfon (a hidden blemish) does not apply to it, because a person does not drink from a cup unless he first examines it; and by a kal vachomer he wishes to reason that in the case of money, too, there is no need to be concerned about a simfon, as [the Gemara] explains.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 10b:15:1.hebrew: זו שביאתה מאכילתה בתרומה - פ"ה: דבנישאת פשיטא דכ"ע מודו דלא חיישינן לסימפון, דאין אדם שותה בכוס אלא א"כ בודקו וידע וקבל עליו. וקשה מה שפירש בקונט' דאיירי בנישאת, דהא לא בא רבינא ליישב אלא דאירוסין עושה. ויש ליישב דה"ק: כי היכי דבנישואין פשיטא ליה דאכלה, דכ"ע מודו דאין אדם שותה בכוס אלא א"כ בודקו, ה"נ אינו בא עליה אלא א"כ בודקה, ואין אדם עושה בעילתו בעילת זנות. והרר"ם פירש דה"ק: מה שפחה כנענית שאין ביאתה מאכילתה בתרומה אפילו מן התורה, כספה מאכילתה אפילו מדרבנן; זו שביאתה מאכילתה מן התורה, אינו דין שכספה מאכילתה אפילו מדרבנן? ומיירי שפיר בביאה שלא ע"י חופה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 10b:15:1.english: "This one, whose intercourse allows her to eat teruma" - Rashi explains that [this refers to a woman who] was married, [for] it is obvious that all agree we are not concerned about simfon, since a person does not drink from a cup unless he examines it, knows [its condition], and accepts it upon himself. But what [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres, that [the Gemara] is speaking of a married woman, is difficult, for Ravina came only to resolve [the case of] betrothal, which does [allow her to eat]. And one can resolve [this] by saying that this is what [Rashi] means: Just as in marriage it is obvious to him [the Tanna] that she eats, since all agree that a person does not drink from a cup unless he examines it, so too here, he does not have relations with her unless he examines her, and a person does not make his act of intercourse an act of harlotry. And Rabbeinu Meir explained that this is what [the Gemara] means: Just as a Canaanite maidservant, whose intercourse does not allow her to eat teruma even by Torah law, [nevertheless] her purchase money allows her to eat even by rabbinic law — this one, whose intercourse allows her to eat by Torah law, is it not logical that her money should allow her to eat, even by rabbinic law? And [the Gemara] speaks properly of intercourse that is not through the wedding canopy.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 10b:5:1.hebrew: ומה שפחה כנענית וכו' זו שביאתה מאכילתה בתרומה אינו דין שכספה מאכילתה - וא"ת ונימא: יבמה תוכיח, שביאתה מאכילתה ואין כספה מאכילתה — אף אני אביא ארוסה? ויש לומר דהאי ק"ו אינו כ"א גלוי מלתא בעלמא, דארוסה מקרי קנין כספו כמו שפחה; הלכך לא שייך למיפרך "יוכיח". עי"ל דליכא למימר "יבמה תוכיח", דאיכא למיפרך: מה ליבמה, שכן אינה נקנית בכסף! תאמר באשה שנקנית בכסף, דין הוא שתאכל בתרומה על ידי כסף:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 10b:5:1.english: "If a Canaanite maidservant...etc. this one, whose intercourse allows her to eat teruma, is it not logical that her money allows her to eat" - And if you say: Let us say, "The yevama will prove [otherwise], for her intercourse allows her to eat [teruma], yet her money does not allow her to eat — so too I will bring the betrothed woman [as a counterexample]"? One can answer that this a fortiori argument is nothing but a mere clarification of the matter, for a betrothed woman is called one acquired by his money, like the maidservant; therefore it is not applicable to refute [it] with "let [the yevama] prove." Alternatively, one can say that one cannot say "the yevama will prove," for one can refute: What of the yevama, which is because she is not acquired through money! Will you say [the same] of a woman who is acquired through money — it is logical that she should eat teruma by means of money.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 10b:5:2.hebrew: מה שפחה כנענית שאין ביאתה מאכילתה - מהאי ק"ו ליכא למילף שתהא אשה נקנית בכסף ובשטר, דאיכא למיפרך: מה לשפחה כנענית, שכן יוצאה בכסף, כדפריך לעיל גבי אמה העבריה. אבל לענין אכילת תרומה לא שייך למיפרך הכי:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 10b:5:2.english: If a Canaanite maidservant, whose intercourse does not allow her to partake [of teruma] - From this a fortiori inference one cannot derive that a woman is acquired through money and through a document, for one can refute it: What [proof is there] from a Canaanite maidservant, since she goes free through money, as [the Gemara] objected above regarding a Hebrew maidservant. But with regard to partaking of teruma, it is not applicable to refute in this way:

Tosafot on Kiddushin 10b:5:3.hebrew: זו שביאתה מאכילתה אינו דין שכספה מאכילתה - וא"ת: ונימא "דיו"? אסוף דינא! כלומר, מאיזה כח אתה בא ללמוד כסף מכח ביאה? דיו כביאה, ולא יאכיל אלא אחר חופה. ודוגמתה בפ"ב דב"ק (דף כה.). וי"ל: הכא סברי כרבי טרפון דאמר לא אמרינן דיו היכא דמיפרך ק"ו, ואי אמרת הכא דיו מיפרך ק"ו. ורבינו שמשון מקוצי תירץ דלא אמרינן דיו אלא היכא דבעי למימר דין חדש, כגון התם דאמר קרן בר"ה חצי נזק, ואתה בא ללמוד נ"ש מק"ו דשן ורגל. אבל הכא דרחמנא אמר קנין כסף אוכל, ואין אנו באין ללמוד מן הק"ו אלא מהו קנין כסף:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 10b:5:3.english: "This one, whose intercourse allows her to eat, is it not logical that her money allows her to eat" - If you say: Let us say "it is sufficient" (dayo) — [that is,] let the conclusion be no greater than its premise! That is to say: from what power do you come to learn [the effect of] money from the power of intercourse? It should be sufficient [for the conclusion] to be like intercourse, and she should eat only after the wedding canopy. And a parallel to this is in the second chapter of Bava Kamma (25a). And one can answer: Here they hold like Rabbi Tarfon, who said that we do not say "it is sufficient" where the a fortiori argument would be refuted [by applying it]; and if you say here "it is sufficient," the a fortiori argument is refuted. And Rabbeinu Shimshon of Coucy answered that we say "it is sufficient" only where one wishes to state a new law, such as there, where [the Torah] said that [damage by] horn in the public domain is half damages, and you come to learn full damages from an a fortiori argument from tooth and foot; but here, where the Merciful One said that acquisition by money allows her to eat, we do not come to learn from the a fortiori argument anything other than what constitutes acquisition by money:
